newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares close weaker but outlook firmer.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares close weaker but outlook firmer.

text.p: Investors were sidelined on Friday by a lack of incentives to ramp up positions in the Singapore stock market, but dealers were hopeful of a return to buying next week.
"It will probably be firmer next week if only because we expect some bargain hunting after this week's weakness," said one dealer with a local firm.
A slow trading day in which 126 million shares changed hands marketwide saw the Straits Times Industrials Index close down 11.89 at 1,955.25.
Morning session gains for property stocks were diminished by the end of play with the Stock Exchange of Singapore property index virtually flat, up just 0.28 at 666.77.
Individually Singapore Land held on to a 15 cent gain to close at Singapore $7.40, while Keppel Land made S$0.14 to end at S$4.34.
Jardine Matheson was the day's biggest gainer, up US$0.20 at US$7.10.
Losers were headed by UOB Bank foreign stock, down 60 cents to S$15.40. Also losing was Venture Manufacturing, down S$0.35 at S$6.65 in active trade.
Small caps dominated the day with Asia Food & Properties seeing almost 12 million shares traded to end the day up US$0.035 at US$0.925, bouncing back from an intra-day low of US$0.855.
